response.title: which portable solar panel charges a power station the fastest in partial shade
response.answer:
For charging a portable power station in partial shade, I'd prioritize solar panels with good shade tolerance and high real-world output, rather than simply buying the panel with the highest advertised wattage.

The key distinction is that some panels lose most of their output when even a small section is shaded, while others can continue producing useful power.

My top recommendation is to look at panels with multiple bypass-diode-protected sections or independently operating modules. If you're willing to carry more than one panel, two smaller panels connected in parallel can sometimes outperform one large panel of the same total wattage in patchy shade.

There's an important caveat: manufacturers rarely publish standardized partial-shade charging tests, so a definitive fastest-panel ranking requires comparable testing under the same conditions.

Best panels to consider
Shop

Renogy ShadowFlux 200W

Best shade-focused option

Designed specifically to reduce partial-shading losses. Renogy claims up to 85% more output in partial shade under its test conditions. However, it's a rigid, portable panel rather than a folding one, and that claim isn't an independent head-to-head result.

200W · About 23.8 lb

Shop

BLUETTI SORA 500

Highest-output folding candidate

A 500W folding panel using a 3-series, 4-parallel cell arrangement. A hands-on review reported good partial-shade handling in some conditions, but substantial losses when central sections were blocked. 
The Verge

500W · About 28.4 lb

Shop

EcoFlow NextGen 220W Bifacial

Best general-purpose 200W-class foldable

Excellent measured output in direct sunlight: OutdoorGearLab reported approximately 193W average in a two-hour test. Its partial-shade performance remains less certain. 
Lab Tested & Ranked

220W · About 15.4 lb

Which actually charges fastest?

Situation

	

My choice




Moving tree shadows, rigid panel acceptable

	

Renogy ShadowFlux 200W




One folding panel, maximum potential watts

	

BLUETTI SORA 500




Lightweight portable setup

	

EcoFlow NextGen 220W




Uneven shade across a larger area

	

Multiple smaller panels on independent MPPT inputs

The power station matters just as much as the panel. Its maximum solar input, voltage limits, and MPPT configuration determine how much of the available energy it can actually capture. 
StormWatts
+1

One question that will change my recommendation

Which power station are you charging? For example, EcoFlow DELTA 2, BLUETTI AC180, Jackery Explorer 1000, or Anker SOLIX C1000.

With the exact model, I can narrow this down to the fastest compatible panel or panel combination for partial shade, rather than just the highest-rated solar panel.
